_comment: kilnCtl bench-fixture known-good config preset. DATA ONLY -- never
compiled into any firmware image (see tools/PcTools/README.md 'Config
presets'). This describes THIS test bench, not a real kiln.
max_temp_c = 80.0 on every zone, and abs_max_temp_c = 80.0 in the
safety section, are FIXTURE ceilings, not kiln limits. They exist
because the bench's heating elements and enclosure are only
rated/instrumented for bench testing at low temperature -- see
firmware/KilnFW/TODO.md 2026-08-28 section ('THE HEATING ELEMENTS ARE
NOW PHYSICALLY CONNECTED') and SaftyFW/TODO.md phase 9 'confirm no
test threshold was left in place'. These 80C values MUST NOT be carried
into a real kiln build/config -- a real kiln's ceiling belongs to that
kiln's own commissioning data, not this file.
Captured 2026-08-27 by reading the live bench board with
kiln_call(name='get_board_state') (read-only) and copying its
control_zones section verbatim, per the owner's request. Reflects: 3
zones, 3 thermocouples, relays 1-3 zone-owned (masks 0x1/0x2/0x4).
relay_count CORRECTED 2026-08-28 from 4 to 3. The original capture took
the number from get_board_state/control_get_zones, whose UART GET_ZONES
reply documents byte2 as 'relay_count (KILN_IO_RELAY_COUNT on this
board)' -- i.e. the HARDWARE constant, 4 relays physically present
(kiln_io.h). The field this preset actually writes is the CONFIG's
relay_count (zones_cfg_t, GET/POST /api/zones), which is 3 on this
bench: how many relays the zones config declares in use
(relay_zone_owned_mask 0x7). Two different quantities, one name. Left
at 4, this preset would have quietly widened the configured relay count
every time it was applied.
sanity_rate_c_per_min = 0.2 on every zone, ADDED 2026-08-29. This is
thermal_guard.c guard 1 (heating-failed / dead element): while the
executor drives a zone below setpoint, the reading must rise at least
this many C per minute over guard_wrong_dir_window_s or the zone trips.
The board carried 5.0 C/min on zone 0, which is a real kiln's figure --
this jig is a small heater against a large thermal mass and takes
MINUTES to move a few degrees, so every step-response and autotune run
died at t=62s with 'heating but rose only 0.0C in 1.0min (need >=5.0C)'
even though all three zones were genuinely heating (owner-confirmed).
0.2 C/min is below this jig's observed rise and still far above zero, so
a genuinely dead element or detached thermocouple -- which produces ~0 --
is still caught, just after a longer window. It is NOT a disable: 0 in
this field means 'use the firmware default 0.5', never 'off'. Only guard
1 reads this number; the runaway, drift, frozen-sensor and absolute-
ceiling guards have their own thresholds and are untouched.
MEASURED 2026-08-29, and 0.2 is NOT yet achievable on this rig. With
guard 1 deliberately held open (rate 0.01, window 1800 s) so only the
plant could end the run, relay 1 stayed closed for 39.8 minutes and zone
0 rose +0.67 C -- 0.017 C/min mean, worst 5-minute window NEGATIVE at
-0.016 C/min. Autotune, run against the same plant, aborted with
'response too small to fit (trace flat or noise-dominated)'. So the
thermal guard was NOT the only blocker: the heat path to zone 0's
thermocouple delivers about nothing, and 0.2 C/min is roughly 12x what
the jig produces. 0.2 is kept here because it is the owner's decision
and it is the right SHAPE of number for a rig that heats; it is left
documented as aspirational rather than quietly lowered to 0.01, which
would make the dead-element guard unable to tell a working element from
a dead one on this bench. Fix the heat path, then re-measure and set
this from data.
name: bench_fixture
description: This bench's known-good starting config: 3 zones, 80C fixture ceiling on all zones, relays 1-3 zone-owned, 3 thermocouples, plus the safety-processor commissioning values this bench can actually vouch for.
_safety_comment: SAFETY-PROCESSOR (SaftyFW) commissioning parameters, written over
SET_PARAM/COMMIT_CONFIG via POST /api/safety/commissioning
(safety_cfg_http_client.py). Every value below is one this bench can
actually vouch for -- read off the live board or off an ESP-side
authority -- because on this link an explicitly-committed value is what
clears calibration_missing (config_store.h: the CONFIG_STORE_SET_* bit,
not the number, is what makes a value 'commissioned'). A plausible
guess written here would not look like a guess afterwards.
tc_source = 0 (OWN_J7)              -- the Pico's own MAX31856 is
fitted (ROADMAP.md: fitted 2026-08-24, verified reading 30.2 C)
and is the sensor it uses. Already committed on this bench.
tc_placement_mode = 0 (CHAMBER_AGREED) -- already committed on this
bench; consistent with tc_source (COMMIT_CONFIG's cross-field
rule only constrains the BORROWED_ZONE case).
abs_max_temp_c = 80.0               -- the fixture ceiling above.
mains_voltage_v = 240.0             -- as committed on this bench.
tc_type = 3 (type K)                -- from the ESP's own authority
for this field, zones_config_get_safety_tc_type(): GET /api/zones
reports safety_tc_type = 3. COMMISSIONING_UX.md sec 1.2 names
that global as where the safety processor's own TC type is
stored, resynced to the Pico by safety_link.c.
max_rate_c_per_min = 0.0            -- 0 means DISABLED, and
CONFIG_REFERENCE.md sec 2 says S8 'ships disabled... enable only
after logging a real full-power ramp'. 0 is the documented
shipped value, not a guess at a rate.
borrowed_zone_index = 0             -- unused while tc_source is
OWN_J7 (CONFIG_REFERENCE.md sec 1: 'only meaningful when
tc_source != OWN_J7'), and 0 is a zone the ESP actually reports,
satisfying that row's own constraint.
ct_installed = 0                    -- ASKED, not derived. NO CT IS
FITTED ON THIS BENCH, and unlike every other field here that is
a fact anyone can confirm by looking at the board rather than a
value inferred from another one. Committing it is what makes
this bench commissionable at all: ct_channel_map stops being
required, and S3/S4/S9/S14 are switched off AND REPORTED off
(safety_guard_state_t::ct_guards_disabled) rather than silently
passing on a sensor that is not there.
NOT PRESENT HERE, deliberately: ct_channel_map[0..2] -- see
_ct_channel_map_retired_comment below. Also absent: k_ct_v_per_a[0..2]
and ct_cal[*], whose only honest producer is the zone current-sweep
(zones_http.c, COMMISSIONING_UX.md sec 1.2), which cannot run without
a CT.
_ct_channel_map_retired_comment: THE ct_channel_map BACKUP SECTION THAT USED TO LIVE HERE IS GONE.
It held an UNVERIFIED identity map (CT channel c -> zone c), opt-in via
use_ct_map_backup=True, and it existed for exactly one reason: this
bench has no CT fitted, ct_channel_map was unconditionally required for
commissioning, and so there was no honest way to reach
commissioning_gate.c's ACCEPT path at all. The map was the least-bad
lie available.
ct_installed = 0 below is the honest answer to the same problem, and it
is a statement this bench can actually back: no current transformer is
clamped around anything (every zone reports ct_mask = 0,
normal_current_a = 0.0, safety_status.current_a = [0,0,0], k_ct_v_per_a
is still 0). Declaring the hardware absent does not claim a mapping
nobody measured; it claims an absence anyone can verify by looking at
the board. So the assumed map is not merely unnecessary now, it is the
wrong shape -- keeping a ready-made unverified map around invites
someone to reach for it.
The use_ct_map_backup=True MECHANISM in config_presets.py is kept: a
board that really does have CTs but whose zone current-sweep cannot
resolve them (two zones sharing one CT, COMMISSIONING_UX.md sec 1.2)
still needs a deliberate, labelled, opt-in manual path. What is retired
is this preset's DATA, not the escape hatch.
TO UN-RETIRE: fit the CTs, set ct_installed = 1, run the zone
current-sweep from the zones page; zone_sweep_push_ct_channel_map()
derives and commits the real, measured map.
